title: POKA / PROJECT P
subtitle: A Solarpunk Open-World Game Concept
summary: A collaborative open-world RPG concept that turns a solarpunk world of high-altitude settlements, ecological signals and shared infrastructure into an explorable interaction system.
statement: Designing the interface between a living planet, a network of builders and the player who connects them.
body:
POKA is a solarpunk anime open-world RPG set on Pracia, a planet where a collective ecological signal intensifies at lower altitudes and drives local creatures into aggression. Human settlements survive above 2,500 metres, while the player—an explorer from the second pioneer fleet—moves between isolated communities to investigate the signal, restore infrastructure and uncover a new answer to the Fermi paradox.

Developed for a Tencent Photon newcomer competition, the project combines exploration, industrial simulation and character-driven storytelling. My contribution focused on translating the team’s world and gameplay systems into player-facing experiences: game concept and mechanics planning, market and user research, HUD and system UI interaction design, and high-fidelity gameplay previsualisation.

blocks.title:
A bright future is
something we build together.
paragraphs: In a genre crowded with ruined futures, POKA begins from optimism: green technology, shared resources and settlements sustained through cooperation rather than extraction.
The player is not a conqueror but a connector. Exploration reveals resources and outposts; restored links allow regional production networks and communities to grow together.

blocks.title:
One world. Multiple
interface states.
blocks.body: I translated exploration, construction, vehicle and combat systems into contextual HUD states. Information density and controls shift with the player’s activity, allowing the interface to support the world instead of sitting on top of it.

blocks.title: From worldbuilding to a playable interface
blocks.body: The final concept connected planning, visual development and 3D previsualisation through one interaction language—giving the team a shared picture of how Pracia would feel in the player’s hands.
